column1: # Issue 1372: the ONE parity table for the dantesync clock-discipline classifier and the date-master
# verdict. BOTH implementations read it: the bash `clock_discipline_class` /
# sourced by scripts/clock-offset-guard.sh) and the python twin `classify_clock_discipline` /
# Columns (TAB-separated): case, status, class, date_verdict (margin 1000 us, micro bound 5 ms),
#   status  = `@<repo-relative path>` to a /status JSON file, or an inline compact JSON object.
#   date_verdict = none (not the date master) | ok | out | paused (a dantesync 1.11.0 master whose
#              micro-corrections are paused: no UTC reading) | unknown (master, fields unreadable)
#   unlocked = yes only for clock_discipline=ptp_phase_lock with ptp_phase_locked=false (the
#              named PTP-PHASE UNLOCKED failure: clock_discipline_unlocked), else no
# The four @ files are /status captured read-only from the live fleet on 26.9.2026 (strih-lx master
# and the stream slave, both dantesync 1.9.0) plus two legacy nodes synthesized from the pre-1.9.0
# field shape (no clock_discipline / ptp_phase_locked / date_* fields).
# The two 1.11.0 @ files (dantesync PR 121, the date micro-corrections) are those two live captures
# extended with the 1.10.0 slew fields and the 1.11.0 micro fields in dantesync's own
# fleet-line error set to what 1.11.0 holds (-2.14 ms). A master that carries
# date_correction_falling_behind is graded on the micro bound (DANTESYNC_DATE_MICRO_BOUND_MS,
# default 5) + margin, falling behind = out, paused = paused; a master without it (1.9.0 / 1.10.0)
# is graded on date_step_bound_ms exactly as before (the mixed fleet during the roll).
